evidence.evidence: Linking checked: linked balise group contained in linking information becomes the position reference, step 1 (BG1 linked, in linking info, report refers to BG1)
Linking checked: balise group not contained in linking information or marked unlinked is not LRBG compliant, step 2 (Scenario B: BG2 unlinked, report still uses BG1)
Linking checked: balise group not contained in linking information or marked unlinked is not LRBG compliant, step 1 (Scenario A: BG2 linked but not in linking info, report still uses BG1)

Linking information released from the transition buffer is applied before SOLR determination, steps 1-2: release at the transition border, replacement before SOLR determination, SOLR is a balise group from the released linking information (may differ from the LRBG). It does not check the DMI/JRU records.

New SSP replaces all stored SSP from its start location, including beyond its end, steps 3-4: the new profile values apply from B and the old SSP is replaced. The generated tests do not verify the DMI display or the JRU recording.
MA request triggered when the train front passes the location a defined time before the perturbation location, steps 2-3: MA request sent with xxx1x set (no JRU/RTM message details)
Single-factor passwords require at least 15 characters, step 1 (14-character password rejected)
Full password is requested and the entire submitted password is verified, steps 3-4 (changed last character and 64-char truncation fail)
Authenticator is disabled after the configured limit (at most 100) of consecutive failures, steps 1-3: repeated failures lead to refusal of further attempts
Authenticator is disabled after the configured limit (at most 100) of consecutive failures, step 2: the authenticator is disabled at the 100th failure; step 3 refuses the valid password afterwards
All authenticators involved in excessive attempts are disabled, step 1: both authenticators are disabled
Disabled authenticator is usable again only after rebinding, steps 1-3: refused before rebinding, succeeds only after rebinding
Every portal page declares its default human language, step 1: html element has a non-empty lang attribute.
Declared language tag has a known primary language subtag, steps 1-2: primary subtag extracted and verified in IANA registry.
Oturum kapatma tüm kimlik doğrulamalı sayfalardan erişilebilir ve oturumu geçersiz kılar, adım 2-3
Oturum sürelerinin güncellenmesi yetkilendirmeye tabidir, adım 1
Oturum etkinlik olmadığında ve geçerlilik süresi dolduğunda sonlanır, adım 3 (oturum kimliği en uzun geçerlilik süresi 8 saat yapılandırılmış ve uygulanıyor)
Oturum etkinlik olmadığında ve geçerlilik süresi dolduğunda sonlanır, adım 2
Parola ya da yetki değişikliğinde etkin oturumlar sonlandırılır, adım 1-2
Oturum kapatma tüm kimlik doğrulamalı sayfalardan erişilebilir ve oturumu geçersiz kılar, adım 4
Test 1 steps 1-2 check the limit of 3 within 15 minutes. Test 2 steps 1-2 check that attempts spread beyond the period do not trigger the limit.
Test 1 step 2 checks automatic locking when the limit is exceeded. Test 3 steps 1-3 check the alternative actions.
Position report references the last passed LRBG compliant balise group, step 1: report uses BG1 as reference (linked BG1 case, though not specifying Q_LINK=1, packet 255, or JRU/period details).
A non LRBG compliant balise group is not used as position reference, step 2: after BG2 (non compliant), report still refers to BG1; unlinked marking not explicitly specified.

Replacement before SOLR determination also applies to linking information released from the transition buffer, step 2 (SOLR determined after release using replaced linking info); only partial, lacking the L2 transition, DMI and JRU specifics, but the core behaviour of SOLR derived after release matches.

New SSP replaces stored SSP from its start location, steps 1 and 3: new SSP is received and the new profile is in effect from B, replacing the old values. The balise/RBC reception and the DMI/JRU recording are not explicitly covered.
Minimum length enforced for single-factor passwords, step 1 (and multi-factor test, step 1)
Authenticator is disabled when the consecutive failed attempt limit is reached, steps 1-2 (failed attempts lead to rate limiting being applied)
Authenticator is disabled when the consecutive failed attempt limit is reached, step 3 (disabled after limit L reached; the exact value of 101 is not specified, but the behaviour is equivalent)
Every portal page declares its default human language, step 1: lang attribute present and not empty on html element.
Kullanıcı oturumu kapattığında oturum sonlanır, adım 1 ve 2
Organization-defined action is taken when the invalid logon limit is exceeded, steps 1-2: N consecutive invalid attempts are rejected and the next one exceeds the limit
Organization-defined action is taken when the invalid logon limit is exceeded, step 2 (account automatically locked) and step 3 (logon refused during lock)
